evidence.reason: `platform-time-error` feeds `now=1e18` into the utilization digest, which `_time` passes to `datetime.fromtimestamp(value, dt.timezone.utc)`. On CPython a failing `gmtime`/`gmtime_s` raises `OSError` whose `str()` embeds the platform errno text; glibc yields `[Errno 75] Value too large for defined data type` (EOVERFLOW), while macOS uses a different errno/message and Windows a different failing branch. The finding's citation of the stored fixture text and of `_capture`/`--check` comparing full regenerated text is consistent with that behavior. So the case is host-dependent even though the family header records only `fractional-zero-offset-is-applied` as host-dependent and claims `--check` holds on every CPython >= 3.14.7 host. That is an ordinary reproducibility defect in the fixture expectation (not merely a documentation-scope request), and recording only the exception kind for this case is the smallest compatible repair.
